且不进一步追究君士坦斯的舰队。显而易见，政府仍向士兵发放军饷，并且主要用金币支付，只是现金军饷改为分期轮发，每三四年才领一次。法律文献提到，士兵既领给养（
annonai
），也领军饷（
rhoga

当然，情况的确有所变化。正如第三章所述，740年代的法律文献有力地表明，自备一部分装备、依靠个人财产的士兵已十分常见。这与假定存在的“农兵”毫无关系。这些证据值得细看片刻，尤其因为它们所描绘的安纳托利亚（至少是帝国核心地区）的变化，与一个多世纪前似乎发生在拉文纳总督辖区的情形极为相似。第一项文献出自8世纪中叶，是对一名士兵和其岳父之间尚待履行的义务所下的裁决。争议的焦点是岳父应就士兵从军所得收入获得多少补偿。裁决的依据是：如果士兵选择离开，实际上就结束了由女婿向家庭收入作出贡献的安排，那么岳父先前为其军用装备所作的投入应当得到补偿。

Without pursuing the matter of Constans’ fleets in further detail, it is clear that soldiers continued to be paid by the government, and largely in gold, even if their cash remuneration was rationalized into a periodic rotation with payments arriving every three or four years. Legal texts refer to the payment of soldiers by both
annonai
and by a
rhoga.

Changes there were, of course, and as noted in Chapter 3, legal texts of the 740s suggest strongly that soldiers who did in fact provide some of their own equipment and were dependent on their own property had become a well-established feature. This has nothing to do with any supposed “farmer-soldiers.” It will be worth dwelling on this evidence for a moment, especially since it suggests a picture of developments in Anatolia, or at least within the core lands of the empire, remarkably similar to those that appear to have taken place in the Ravenna exarchate over a century earlier. The first text, dated to the middle of the eighth century, is a decision regarding outstanding obligations on the part of a soldier and his wife’s father. The issue revolves around the level of compensation the latter is to receive in respect of the soldier’s earnings from his military service. The ruling is based on the recognition that, should the soldier opt to leave, thus effectively terminating the arrangement through which the son-in-law contributed to the household income, then his father-in-law should be compensated in respect of his investment in the soldier’s military gear.
741年颁行的《法律选编》（
Ecloga
）第十六篇第二条处理了一个类似情形。条文涉及兄弟共同继承父母的地产和家业。
全文值得引录：
Chapter xvi, 2 of the
Ecloga,
issued in 741, treats a comparable situation. Here the text concerns brothers who inherit a parental estate and household with joint ownership.
It is worth quoting the text in full:

父母亡故后，若遗有数名兄弟，一人服兵役，另一人留在家中劳作，双方如有约定，应依其约定。若未作约定，但自该兄弟从军之日起到满十年一直共同生活，则所有所得，无论来自军饷［rhoga］，还是来自留在地产上的兄弟一人或数人辛勤劳作，均应平分。如果他们于这十年之后又共同生活三年才分家，士兵得保有其马与鞍具和武器；若已添置甲胄，也得保有；其余财产则应在兄弟间公平分配。若共同生活超过这十三年，士兵在此之后仍存有军饷，则也归其本人保有。

If brothers are left after the decease of their parents and one of them is in military service while the other remains active in the household, then, if they have made an agreement, that which was agreed should remain in force. But if they make no agreement but live together for up to ten years from the beginning of the military service of the said brother, then everything that they have acquired, whether from the pay [rhoga] or the exertions and the hard work of the brother or brothers remaining on the estate should be divided in equal parts. But if they live for a further three years together after these ten years and then separate, then the soldier shall keep his horse with its harness and his weapons, and also his armor, should he have acquired one; but everything else should be apportioned between them in a brotherly fashion. And if they live together longer than these thirteen years and the soldier still has after this time something from his pay, then he should retain this also.
军中所得显然被视作共有收入的一部分，与此同时，家户也被认为为士兵提供了供养。
士兵的坐骑和军用装备，须在经过一定年限后才不列入分家财产。这意味着其他兄弟原本有权主张这些财物。由此可见，服役所需的装备是基于国家利益才免于分割的。但没有理由认为，家户曾负有供养士兵的义务。制定这一条文的法学家显然认识到，须就头十年内家产所失的收益和作出的投入予以补偿。超过十年后，则认定士兵的收入已足以弥补家户供养他的开支，因此他可以留下马匹和其他装备。十三年期满后，他对家户所负的债务即告消灭。
It seems apparent that the military income was included as part of the common income, and that the soldier was by the same token understood to be supported by the household.

The soldier’s mount and military gear are excluded from the division of property, but only after a certain period, which assumes that the other brother(s) had a claim on them. The equipment necessary to military service was thus exempted in the interests of the state. But there is no reason to think that the household had been obliged to support the soldier. The lawyers who designed the ruling clearly recognized the necessity of compensating the estate for its loss of income and its contribution up to a period of ten years. After this point, the soldier’s income was taken to have recompensed the household for his maintenance, and he retained horse and other gear, until, after a period of thirteen years, his debt to his household was extinguished.
这两项文献表明，家户可以供养士兵。提供供养的一方有权从此前不可动用的军役特有财产（
peculium
）中请求补偿，这一权利使他们的投入得到正式承认。由此可见，关于军役特有财产（
peculium
）的传统规定已经改变，关于如何负担军费的基本认识也发生了重要转变。
这些裁决可能反映了曾呈报朝廷的一些个案，显示士兵的家庭或家户对其服役所作的投入可以折算，在原有安排发生变化时也就可以予以补偿。这意味着供养和维持野战军士兵的办法，与此前大不相同。
这也反映出这些军队中相当大的一部分在逐渐变成近于民兵的力量。它们仍可参加大型远征并有效作战，却越来越以所属行省为依托，或许已类似阿拉伯入侵前旧有的边防军（
limitanei
）。顺带一提，那些部队后来的下落，我们几乎一无所知。

These two texts indicate that households could support soldiers but that this contribution had been formally recognized in the right of the contributing parties to make a claim on the hitherto untouchable military
peculium
for recompense. This in turn shows that the traditional regulations pertaining to military
peculium
had been modified and suggests a significant shift in assumptions about how the military was financed.

The decisions probably reflect cases that had come to the attention of the imperial court at some point, and they demonstrate that the soldier’s family or household supported his military service in a way that could be quantified, and thus could be compensated when the arrangement changed. It implies a rather different arrangement for maintaining and supporting soldiers in field armies than had hitherto been in force

and reflects one aspect of the slow transformation of a large part of these armies into a more militia-like force, still capable of participating in major expeditions and in effective military action but increasingly provincialized— perhaps resembling the older
limitanei
units of the period before the Arab invasions (about whose fate, incidentally, we know virtually nothing).
这一变化在多大程度上源于驻省军队领饷不如从前规律，或行省经济货币化程度降低，或政府蓄意减轻国库直接负担的政策，仍不清楚。士兵继续领取金币，但发放间隔反映出财政愈加窘迫。例如，一份10世纪的文献称，地方部队按四年一轮的传统领取军饷，另有一些9世纪的阿拉伯语记载说是三年一轮。有学者认为，政府借此应付投放流通的金币暂时减少。现在对7世纪后半叶铸币发行的分析证实，这种减量确实存在。
不过，轮流发饷很难有助于负担军队的日常维持费用，尤其是640年代以后，野战军似乎已按前文所述的方式分驻各行省。给驻省部队发饷的间隔延长，时间一久，很可能促使一部分士兵，甚至很多士兵，在日常供养和军备的某些方面更多地依赖自家。

To what extent this shift reflected a less regularly salaried provincial military, a less monetized provincial economy, or a planned policy on the part of the government to reduce the costs falling directly on the fisc remains unclear. Soldiers continued to be paid in gold, but at intervals that reflected a more straitened fiscal economy. A tenth-century text, for example, describes the traditional method of paying the provincial armies as based on a four-yearly cycle (or a three-yearly cycle, as described by some ninth-century Arabic accounts), and it has been suggested that this was how the government dealt with the temporarily reduced availability of gold coinage put into circulation— a real reduction, as evidenced now by the analysis of coinage-emissions for the second half of the seventh century.

But this rotational system can hardly have helped with the normal maintenance costs of the armies, especially when, from the 640s, the field armies seem to have been distributed across the provinces according to the pattern already discussed, and the less frequent payments to provincial forces may well over time have encouraged some— perhaps many—to place a greater degree of dependence upon their families for some aspects of their support and equipment.
尽管军人服役与家户的关系日益密切，军队仍须大体沿用既定的供给方式，由行省居民遵照征调或强制收购的要求，把定量的谷物、其他农产品及牲畜送抵主要收集点。无论流通中的铜质小额钱币有多少，各类物资、给养和军备都必须定期供应。在具体管理层面，主要凭借有关官员留下的铅印，我们可以隐约看出物资购买、集中和再分配的办法发生了几项重要变化。其中一些变化，似乎与商业官（
kommerkiarioi
）逐渐发挥的作用以及旧有大区行政部门地位的下降相吻合，这里无须深究。维持驻省军队、为其提供补给的既有制度，基本架构仍然在运作，但除了某些经办官员的姓名，几乎没有关于其实际运作的直接证据。然而，一旦筹备出征或组织反击，往往必须在很短时间内准备远超平时的物资。商业官（
kommerkiarioi
）可能为此提供便利。假如最初确是沿用晚期罗马既有的做法，以强制收购获得物资，这项假说就更能说得通。618年后，君士坦丁堡的供给方式逐步变化，商业官（
kommerkiarioi
）在其中发挥了关键作用。君士坦丁堡政府在现金及其他收入减少时，因事制宜地利用了这套逐步成形的安排，把既有架构延伸到新的职能领域，巧妙维持了包括军队在内的各项活动。向各地驻军轮流发饷，即使无法降低养兵的总成本，也有助于压低年度开支。这种办法还可能使许多士兵更倾向于、甚至不得不依靠自己的家户供养，从而进一步减轻了国库的负担。政府以此应对危局，成效相当显著。

Regardless of this increasing association between the service of military personnel and their households, the armies still had to rely largely on the established pattern of support, by which provincials delivered certain quantities of grain and other produce as well as livestock to key points for collection, whether following requisitions or compulsory purchase. And regardless of the amount of bronze petty coinage in circulation, supplies, provisions, and matériel had to be provided on a regular basis. At the level of micromanagement we can detect somewhat dimly and largely through the evidence of lead seals of the relevant officials some important shifts in the ways resources were purchased, collected and redistributed. By the same token, we can see how some of these shifts might fit into the emerging pattern of activities of the
kommerkiarioi

and the declining importance of the old prefectural administration, although we do not need to pursue those issues now. The bare bones of the established infrastructure for maintaining and supplying armies in the provinces continued to function, although we have little direct evidence for how this worked apart from the names of some of the officials associated with it. When a campaign was planned, however, or a defensive counterattack organized, a much greater quantity of matériel was required, and often very quickly, and the hypothesis that it was the
kommerkiarioi

who may have facilitated this seems to fit, the more so if we accept that this was achieved at first through compulsory purchases, following the established late Roman pattern. Building on an ad hoc basis upon the gradual shifts in arrangements for supplying Constantinople in the period after 618, in which the
kommerkiarioi

had come to play a key role, we can see how the government at Constantinople cleverly exploited these developing arrangements to support its activities, including its armies, in a time of reduced cash and other revenues by expanding an established framework into new areas of activity. Paying the provincial armies on a cyclical basis would have contributed to a reduction in annual costs, if not to the overall total cost of maintaining them; while this might also have encouraged a tendency— a need— for many to become more dependent on their immediate households for support, thus similarly lightening the burden on the fisc.
It was crisis management, but it was crisis management that worked remarkably well.

此处可以回到第六章谈到的几项环境证据。前面已经看到，花粉资料显示，在7世纪中后期的安纳托利亚，简化的农业体制在许多地区颇具代表性。不过，很难处处判定这是环境压力造成的，还是人为作用的结果，例如市场需求带来的经济压力、战事及治安恶化，或其他原因。这个过程与任何明显的环境变动都不相符，而且似乎发生在不同地区、不同时间，历时也各不相同。在安纳托利亚的一些地方，例如帕夫拉戈尼亚和本都一带或比提尼亚，传统混合农业延续下来，与新兴的简化体制并存。因此，尽管记录零散，这种格局也并非完全由数据缺漏所致。更重要的是，这提示我们，当时的农人有一定选择余地。同一环境区内，有些人选择采用与原有体制不同的做法，其他人则维持原状。下文将讨论这些选择背后可能的动机。

This is an appropriate point at which to reintroduce some of the issues broached in Chapter 6 regarding the environmental evidence. We have seen that the palynological data suggest that a simplified agrarian regime was representative of many regions of Anatolia from the middle and later seventh century but that it is not always clear whether this was the result of environmental pressure or reflects human agency— economic pressure reflecting market demand, for example; insecurity and warfare; or other causes. The process does not coincide with any obvious environmental shift and indeed seems to take place over different periods, at different times, and in different regions. In some parts of Anatolia, such as Paphlagonia-Pontus or Bithynia, the traditional mixed agriculture continues and coexists with the new simplified regime so that, although the record is patchy, this picture is not just a reflection of a lacunose dataset. Importantly, it also suggests that we have to do here with an element of choice: some farmers within the same environmental zone chose to adopt a different regime from the established system; others did not. We will discuss the possible motives behind these choices below.
Feeding Mars

把以上几方面的变化放在一起，或许可以解释其中的一部分。首先须考虑自650年代起政府陷入的财政困局。供养军队所需的资源是首要事项，因为这一时期军队显然始终在各省活动。它们收复被阿拉伯军队夺占的战略据点、堡垒和城镇，重新加固防御，尾追并袭扰敌军分遣队，维持帝国的存在。同一时期财政体系的变化，无论涉及基本土地税的管理，还是为帝国军队筹办给养和装备，都体现了这些关切。财政用语的变化同样可以看出征收方式的转变：由征收现金，改为以实物满足军队所需资源中大得多的一部分，而且主要收取谷物。这些谷物供分驻帝国各省的军队作战之用，储存在帝国的仓库（
apothēkai
）里，其征集方式使传统上表示强制收购的术语，逐渐有了定期按年征派的含义。

A possible explanation for some of these changes may be sought by bringing together the developments I have now sketched out. First, let us consider the desperate financial straits in which the government found itself from the 650s onward. Resources to supply the armies were a priority because it is quite clear that the armies remained active in the provinces throughout this period, reoccupying and refortifying strong-points, fortresses, and cities seized by the Arabs, dogging and harassing enemy detachments, and maintaining the presence of the imperial state. The changes in the fiscal system that can be detected across the same period, both in respect of the management of the basic land tax as well as in respect of raising supplies and equipment for the imperial armies, reflect these concerns, just as the changes in fiscal terminology can be shown to reflect a shift from raising tax in cash to raising a much greater proportion of the resources required for the armies in kind, predominantly in the form of grain, grain that was intended to support the operations of armies widely dispersed across the provinces of the empire, grain that was stored in imperial depositories or
apothēkai,
and grain that was collected in a way that meant that the traditional term for a compulsory purchase came to have the meaning of a regular and annual imposition.

其次，从7世纪中叶开始，东罗马世界的贸易和商业环境发生了剧变。两者当然都没有完全中止。考古资料，尤其是陶器流通的证据，清楚表明跨越政治边界的交换贯穿了自630年代至9世纪乃至更晚的战争时期。但交换格局随形势而变。流入内陆的外国货物不如从前多。中短程沿海贸易和沿岸航运延续下来，但随着生产中心变动，运载的货物和陶器也换了种类。一些长途贸易也延续下来，却无疑受到7世纪后半叶政局变化的影响。新路线开辟，旧路线改道，许多路线大概就此废弃。若干商品的市场需求变了，运货的途径也变了，海路运输有时必然比通常更危险。当时留下的直接资料很少，但从前往圣地的朝圣者的记载等材料可知，旅行确实并未绝迹。然而，这些剧烈变化，加上若干地区近乎无休止的战争，一定大大影响了面向市场的农业生产。为销售而种植作物的地主、农场经营者和农民，会一如既往地停止种植市场上已无需求的作物，转而种植仍有销路的作物。如果到730年为止，商业官（
kommerkiarioi
）确实负责按定价或市价进行大宗现金采购，以维持国家运转，那么他们的活动很可能进一步推动了这种调整。

Second, there was a dramatically changed situation with regard to trade and commerce in the east Roman world from the middle of the seventh century. Neither entirely ceased, of course, and it is clear from the archaeological data, in particular from the movement of ceramics, that exchange across political borders continued throughout the period of warfare from the 630s into the ninth century and beyond. The patterns of exchange evolved to match the new circumstances, however— fewer international products reached inland regions than before, and short- and medium-distance coastal trade and cabotage continued, but the types of goods and ceramics that were carried changed as the centers of production changed. Some long-distance trade also continued, but it was certainly affected by the changed political circumstances of the second half of the seventh century, with the establishment of new routes, the diversion of older ones, and the probable closure of many. Market demand for some commodities changed, the options for moving goods around changed, and the transport of goods by sea must on occasion have been more hazardous than usual. We have little direct information from this period, but some travel certainly continued, as we know from the accounts of pilgrims to the Holy Land, for example. Nevertheless, such dramatic shifts combined with the impact of almost constant warfare in some regions must have impacted market-orientated agricultural production considerably. Landowners, farmers, and peasant producers who grew crops for a market would have responded in the way that they have always done by ceasing to grow those items no longer in demand and turning to those that were. Such a response may well have been given added stimulus by the activities of the
kommerkiarioi
in the period up to 730, if it was indeed the case that they were responsible for substantial cash purchases, whether at fixed prices or the market rate, to support the state’s activities.
第三，恰恰从670年代初起，商业官（
kommerkiarioi
）标有小纪年的铅印开始大量出现。印上的纪年指十五年周期中的某一年。有人将其与财政管理若干方面的重要变化联系起来，进而联系到军需供应办法的变化。这个解释颇为合理，尽管细节仍不清楚。

最后，由于缺乏适当数据，无法作出有统计意义的量化估计。不过，自6世纪后半叶起，东罗马帝国人口显然大幅下降。这既是鼠疫长期流行的结果，也源于这一时期断续波及帝国各地的战乱和流离。考古资料中聚落分布的变化，可以让我们窥见一些迹象。疫病通常在沿海地区、人口密集的城市和村落造成比在人口稀疏的内陆地区更大的冲击，尽管也有例外。这样一来，帕夫拉戈尼亚和本都等沿岸地区的人口损失就很可能超过内地。帕夫拉戈尼亚的花粉资料或许正反映了这一点：谷物生产强度明显下降，但谷物相对于传统各类作物的比重却上升了。
人手匮乏显然影响了军队，也必定影响了劳动力的供应。人们通常推断，这意味着农业产量下降，这是合理的。
Third, it is precisely from the early 670s that the lead seals of
kommerkiarioi

bearing an indictional date (a year within a given fifteen-year cycle) begin to appear in quantity, a change that has been plausibly associated with an important change in some aspects of fiscal management (even if the details thereof remain obscure) and hence with the ways in which military supplies were managed.

And, finally, while a statistically useful quantification is not possible owing to the absence of appropriate data, it is clear that the eastern Roman state was suffering a substantial demographic decline from the second half of the sixth century onward, an effect of endemic plague as well as of the warfare and dislocation that affected different regions of the empire on and off across the period and that can be glimpsed in the archaeological evidence for shifts in the settlement pattern. Epidemics generally impacted on coastal regions, urban concentrations, and village communities to a greater extent than less well-populated inland districts, although this is not invariably so. But it might well have meant a higher demographic cost in coastal regions, such as Paphlagonia and the Pontus, than inland, and it may well be this that is reflected in the palynological data for Paphlagonia, with a clear reduction in the intensity of grain production on the one hand, yet a proportional increase in cerealiculture compared with the suite of traditional crops.

Manpower shortages affected the army, that much is clear; but they must also have affected the availability of labor, and it is generally— and reasonably— assumed that this meant a reduction in agrarian output.

鉴于这几点，我们不禁要问：大致在上述变化发生的同时，也就是7世纪后半叶，安纳托利亚各地的栽培重点从传统的谷类、坚果、葡萄和橄榄混种，转向刚才所说的“简化”种植，这会是巧合吗？在东地中海的文化背景下，传统作物仍是“必需品”。但即使在沿海，橄榄油和葡萄酒等产品大概也已没有7世纪初以前那样广阔的市场。第六章提及的几个地区的花粉记录显示，葡萄和橄榄等作物相对于谷物的比重明显下降。当时看不出有明显的气候因素或环境变化。

In light of these points, we must ask whether it can be a coincidence that at very roughly the same time as these developments— the second half of the seventh century—we see a change in emphasis across Anatolia from the established mixed crop of cereals, nuts, vines, and olives to the “simplified” crop just described. The traditional crops were still “essentials” in an eastern Mediterranean cultural context, but even along the coastal regions, products such as olive oil and wine probably no longer enjoyed the expansive market of the years before the earlier seventh century. A clear reduction in the proportion of crops such as vines and olives as against cereals is observable in the pollen records from several of the areas noted in Chapter 6, at a time when no obvious climatic factor or shift in conditions was present.
无论如何，橄榄的种植大体取决于气候，尤其是冬季气温。严冬时气温降到约零下10至13摄氏度，橄榄树就会枯死。安纳托利亚通常不能在海拔约1000米以上栽培橄榄树，因此只有地势较低的地方和沿海地区才能种植。
总体而言，大规模橄榄种植似乎在晚期罗马时代之后有所退缩。
例如，到10、11世纪，安纳托利亚的橄榄油生产局限于沿海地区和比提尼亚。一位11世纪的著述者说，离海超过60公里（37英里，300
stadia
）便不再有人种植橄榄。
这在多大程度上反映了市场需求、生产者人口锐减或种植橄榄所需的气候条件变化，仍不清楚。就锡诺普一带而言，如第六章所述，至少按目前掌握的情况，第二种解释更为可能。
同理，到了9、10世纪，安纳托利亚显然已被视为主要的谷物供应地，特别是本都沿海平原及高原北缘紧邻沿海的腹地。
中程和较远程市场的变动，特别是橄榄油和葡萄酒等产品的市场变动，对从事这些生产的人以及在海岸或近海地区经营的人，影响更为直接。相比之下，内陆生产者除少数例外，几乎完全以自给和供应邻近腹地的城乡聚落为目的。

Olive cultivation is in any case determined largely by climatic factors and by winter temperatures in particular. Severe winter temperatures, in the order of −10°C to −13°C, will wither and kill the tree. Olive tree cultivation in Anatolia cannot usually take place above ~1000 masl, so that successful olive cultivation is restricted to lower elevations and coastal regions.
In general, the extensive cultivation of the olive does seem to have regressed after the late Roman period,

and by the tenth and eleventh centuries olive oil production in Anatolia was restricted to coastal regions and Bithynia, for example, while an eleventh-century commentator notes that olives are not cultivated further than 60 km/ 37 miles (300
stadia
) from the sea.

It remains unclear to what extent this reflected market demand, a demographic collapse of the producing population, or was a response to shifts in the climatic conditions required for olive production. For the Sinope region, as noted in Chapter 6, the second factor is more likely, at least in the current state of our knowledge.

By the same token, it is clear that by the ninth and tenth centuries Anatolia, and particularly the Pontic coastal plains and immediate hinterland on the northern edge of the plateau, were seen as major suppliers of grain.

The shifts in both medium- and longer-distance markets, especially for produce such as olive oil and wine, will have affected those engaged in those areas of production as well as those on or near the coasts more directly than inland producers who, with some few exceptions, were producing almost entirely for subsistence needs and the provisioning of local settlements, both urban and rural, in their immediate hinterland.
一般来说，种植谷物的收益远低于种植橄榄、葡萄等作物，少有例外，比如饥荒造成谷物短缺。因此，只要条件适宜且有销路，农人自然更愿意种植后者。
要推动谷物种植相对于其他商品作物有所扩张，即使土地本身适合种谷物，也须有一定的推动力。它可能来自市场需求，也可能另有来源。小麦除了需要适宜的土壤和地形，每年还需要大约300毫米的降水。安纳托利亚许多地方都容易满足这些条件。该地区的数据清楚表明，自6世纪开始进入较湿润的阶段后，原先条件欠佳的地区也很可能达到了这一要求。这些恰好就是有利于提高谷物种植比重的条件，而花粉资料似乎也显示了这一变化。

Now cereal crops offer in general a considerably lower return (except in unusual circumstances, such as famine shortage, for example) than those such as olives and vines, so it is not surprising that where the conditions were appropriate and a market was available farmers preferred the latter.

To promote the (relative) expansion of cerealiculture instead of other marketable produce (assuming that the land itself was suitable for cereal production) required, therefore, some pressure, either from the market in terms of demand, or from another source. In addition to the appropriate soils and surfaces, wheat requires some 300 mm annual precipitation. These are conditions that are readily found in many regions of Anatolia, and after the onset of the wetter phase from the sixth century, as indicated very clearly in the data for the region, were likely also present in areas hitherto less well-endowed (see Map 6.1 for modern Anatolian rainfall patterns). These were precisely the conditions that would have facilitated the relative increase in grain production that the pollen data appear to suggest.

政府通过分驻各地的军队对谷物、牲畜和其他资源提出的需求，整个帝国都会感受到。更重要的是，正如前文所述，大约从7世纪中叶起，野战军已分驻安纳托利亚各地，以便更好地满足军队需要，同时也有利于有效抵御阿拉伯人的袭扰和入侵。这样的调动必然大大增加了许多地区供应驻军的负担，与此同时也扩大了军中所需食品和其他物资的销路。驻军给当地生产者带来的额外负担可能很重。以下简要分析几个例子，说明负担有多大，并考虑它意味着什么。关于古代和中世纪军队所需基本供给，现已有不少研究。士兵每日口粮的一些平均数已获得普遍认同，虽总有少许误差。比如，从古罗马到晚期罗马及拜占庭，士兵每日需要700克至1.2千克（1.54—2.6磅）谷物。取平均值时，约1千克（2.2磅）是偏低的估计。当然，除谷物或面包外，视所在地点和具体情况，士兵还可能分到一份油、葡萄酒以及一些奶酪或腌肉。
7世纪的证据与此相符。630和640年代，新驻叙利亚、巴勒斯坦和埃及的穆斯林士兵，除油、醋和蜂蜜之外，在埃及每人每日还可领两至三磅小麦（并非烤好的面包），在叙利亚则稍少。
10世纪一部拜占庭军事论著称，士兵的基本口粮是面包配奶酪或腌制的肉干。
撇开小幅差异，这些数字可以用来大体估算士兵对谷物的需求。例如，一支约三百人的部队每年需要约11万千克面包，须用约12万至13万千克尚未磨制的小麦。

The demands from the government, exerted through its armies in the provinces, for grain, livestock, and other resources will have been felt throughout the empire. More significantly, and as we have now seen, it is clear that from sometime around the middle of the seventh century the field armies had been distributed across Anatolia, the better to accommodate their requirements, as well as to facilitate an effective defensive response to the Arab raids and invasions. Such a move will have considerably increased the burden on many regions to provide supplies for these troops, while at the same time creating an expanded market for the sale of the foodstuffs and other supplies they required. The additional burden on the producing population of an area where soldiers are based can be very heavy, and it will be worth examining briefly some examples to demonstrate the nature of this and to consider its implications. A good deal of work has now been done on the basic supplies required for armies in the ancient and medieval world, and some average figures for the daily rations of a soldier are generally agreed, although there is always a small margin of error. Thus, the daily grain requirements for a Roman soldier and for his late Roman and Byzantine counterpart ranges from 700 g to 1.2 kg (1.54–2.6 lbs.), with about 1 kg (2.2 lbs.) as a low estimated average. In addition to the grain or bread, of course, soldiers might also receive a portion of oil, wine, and some cheese or salted meat, depending on location and context.

Seventh-century evidence supports this— newly installed Muslim soldiers in Syria, Palestine, and Egypt in the 630s and 640s received a daily ration of between 2–3 lbs. of wheat (rather than baked bread) in Egypt, and somewhat less in Syria, in addition to an allowance of oil, vinegar, and honey.
In the tenth century a Byzantine military treatise describes the basic soldier’s ration as consisting of bread with either cheese or dried salted meat.

Regardless of the minor variations, however, these figures permit some more general calculations about the grain requirements of soldiers. A unit of some three hundred soldiers, for example, would need an annual supply of some 110,000 kg of bread, requiring something in the order of 120,000–130,000 kg of wheat before grinding.

还可以十分粗略地估计，要达到这一产量需要多少土地，从中了解维持一支驻军对土地和当地生产者的总体负担。依据关于意大利、希腊、巴尔干和近东的多种古代及中世纪资料推算，以偏低的平均值计，小麦的播种量与收获量之比约为1∶4或1∶5，每公顷约产520千克（即每英亩208千克），每公顷播种130千克（每英亩52千克）。大麦的估计产量则为每公顷770千克（即每英亩308千克）。这些产量确实比较低。晚期罗马和拜占庭时期现有的文字证据很有限，估计得保守一些是合理的，但产量若不及播种量的四倍，几乎就没有可供出售的余粮。
有关安纳托利亚和巴尔干作物产量的文献显示，在中等质量的土壤和不灌溉的农业条件下，播种量与收获量之比约为1∶3.5至1∶5。湿润或有灌溉的地区产量更高，可达播种量的八九倍。
中世纪晚期和近代早期意大利的收获量，根据湿润或干燥的地区而异，低时是播种量的三四倍，高时为八至十倍。1940年代以前的土耳其则在五至九倍之间。因此，可以把这些数值视作更大范围内的平均水平，假定其间各小区域有所差异。

It is possible to make some very approximate calculations of how much land was required to generate this return and thus offer some idea of what the overall cost to the landscape and to the producing population was in respect of maintaining a military force in its area. Calculations based on a range of ancient and medieval sources for Italy, Greece, the Balkans, and the Near East suggest that a low average return on seed sown to yield would have been in the region of 1:4 or 1:5 for wheat, with a per hectare production of approximately 520 kg (i.e., 208 kg per acre) and a sowing rate of 130 kg/ha (52 kg/acre). For barley rates of 770kg/ ha (i.e., 308 kg/acre) have been proposed. These are indeed comparatively low yields, and while a conservative estimate is justified by the very limited evidence currently available (from texts) for the late Roman and Byzantine periods, a return of less than 1:4 would barely generate a marketable surplus.

Documents relating to crop yields for Anatolia as well as the Balkans indicate returns on sowing of some 1:3.5 to 1:5 on soils of medium quality and in non-irrigation agriculture conditions, with higher rates in wet or irrigated areas—as much as 1:8–9.

Since the variations for Italy in the later medieval and early modern periods range from yields of 1:3–4 to 1:8–10, and in pre-1940s Turkey from 1:5–9, depending on zone (wet or dry), we may take them as averages across a wider terrain with an assumed range of variable subareas.
不过，仍须谨慎。中世纪到奥斯曼时期，技术似乎很少有变化，木犁直到1960年代仍是耕地的主要工具。在这个背景下，奥斯曼晚期和土耳其共和国早期的资料虽显示平均产量起伏很大，但多数年份的小麦和大麦产量，仍高于古代和中世纪铭文及其他文字资料给出的数值。这一点颇值得留意。

例如，1909—1914年，乔鲁姆省小麦的实际产量，往往是据中世纪材料预计的三四倍。根据现有证据粗估，即使种收之比只有1∶5，13万千克小麦也只需约250公顷（617.7英亩）耕地。丰年产量大幅提高，种收之比或达1∶10，同样面积的土地就能产出两倍的粮食，三百名士兵便只需要约125公顷（309英亩）土地的收成。如果他们还是骑兵，则另需数量相近的大麦等精饲料，以及牧草。三百匹马全年每天需要约四五小时的放牧时间，或同等数量的干草，每年约合2,225公顷（5,500英亩）牧地。当然，一支三百人的部队可能拥有多达一千匹马，其中包含备用和替换的坐骑。

We do need to be cautious, however. In view of the fact that there appears to have been remarkably little technological change between the medieval and Ottoman periods— the wooden plow was still the chief instrument of arable tillage into the 1960s—it is significant that, while the evidence from late Ottoman and early Turkish Republic sources indicates considerable variability in average yields, nevertheless in most years the yields for wheat and barley are greater than those offered by the ancient and medieval inscriptional and textual sources.

Thus, yields of wheat within the province of Çorum for the years from 1909– 1914, for example, were often three or four times expected values based on medieval sources. A very rough estimate based on the available evidence would suggest that, at a rate of return of just 1:5, 130,000 kg of wheat represents some 250 hectares (617.7 acres) of arable. In a good year with a much higher yield— perhaps 1:10— the same acreage would have produced twice this amount, so the three hundred soldiers would have needed the harvest from some 125 hectares (309 acres). Assuming these were also cavalry soldiers, then similar amounts of hard fodder such as barley, plus grazing, would be required— three hundred horses would need something in the order of four to five hours per day or its equivalent in hay around the year, which amounts to some 2,225 hectares (5,500 acres) per annum. And of course a unit of three hundred soldiers would probably have up to one thousand horses at their disposal, to include spare mounts and replacements, for example.
同样粗略估算，660年代驻扎在亚美尼亚孔地区的部队，假定共有一万五千人，每年就需要约547.5万千克面包，相当于多达600万千克小麦。
尚未计入马匹所需的精饲料和干饲料，也就是大麦和干草。考虑到季节性病虫害及异常强降雨或霜冻造成的损失，实际所需的土地应是这一数值的数倍。
还须记得，人口下降会使实际耕种的总面积缩小。即便如此，只要分驻各地的兵力安排妥当，尽量减轻任何一处地方的负担，
这一数量也完全在构成该区域的各行省所能生产的小麦范围内。正如前文所见，当时的确作了这样的安排。

On the basis of a similarly crude calculation, therefore, the military forces based in the Armeniakon region in the 660s— assuming a total manpower of fifteen thousand— would have required some 5,475,000 kg of bread per annum, representing up to 6 million kgs of wheat,
in turn representing the product of a consolidated area of some 5,200–5,300 hectares (12,800–13,100 acres)

of arable, in addition to the requirement in hard and dry fodder— barley and hay— for the horses. The amount of land actually required would in fact have been several times greater than this, in light of the impact of losses incurred through seasonal diseases and pests as well as unusually heavy rainfall or frosts.

Additionally, it should be recalled that demographic decline would have reduced the overall total of cultivated arable. Nevertheless, such a quantity is well within the wheat-growing capacity of the provinces that made up that region, providing that the soldiers were appropriately distributed to minimize the burden on any particular locality
—as we have now seen they were.

Agricultural output can, under the right circumstances, respond fairly rapidly to shifts in the market, and in particular to demand from the military, as examples from both the ancient and late Roman worlds as well as more recent history amply demonstrate,

or as illustrated by the market-orientated cash crop in olives and wine as well as mixed farming that drove the agrarian commerce of North Africa and the limestone massif in northern Syria in the fifth and first half of the sixth century.

In Apulia in the course of the later fourth and fifth centuries, for example, landowners and producers progressively turned over an ever greater proportion of their output to cereals in response both to market demand and the possibilities for greater profits as well as state fiscal pressure.

In the late third century the Roman Republic was able to increase grain production over a very short period through fiscal pressure, increasing rents in kind and exploiting the market opportunities offered to private landowners through higher prices; while in the second and third centuries the demands of the state for supplies for the army as well as other consumers impacted directly on levels of production of both private landlords and peasant taxpayers as well as imperial estates.

There are many examples from the ancient world for peasant farmers, whether tenants or not, and landowners responding to both market opportunities generated by the presence of military forces as well as to fiscal pressure to meet state demands for grain, livestock, and similar produce for local military units.
Indeed, where a guaranteed market was accessible, landowners could increase production of the crops in demand in order to ensure their income as well as to make a profit.

军队最需要的是谷物和牲畜。牲畜既用于运输，如马、骡和驴，也用于供给食物，如牛、绵羊和山羊及其乳制品。军队还需要葡萄酒、油、奶酪等其他日常用品。因此，从640和650年代起，安纳托利亚各省的驻军需求增加，花粉资料显示上一章所述的、以谷物种植和畜牧为主的简化混合体制在此期间扩张，也就不必惊讶了。几项因素同时出现，提示了一种解释。一方面，考古记录清楚表明，过去相当依赖国际市场销售专门产品，尤其是葡萄酒、橄榄及橄榄油的地区，面临需求大幅缩减。轻微的气候变化或会使传统农业难以维系，甚至无法继续，尽管如前所见，上一章讨论的代用数据并未表明当时的安纳托利亚发生了这种变化。与此同时，许多地方来了比以往更多的士兵，而且多少成了常驻，这就提高了对小麦等农产品和牲畜的需求。因此，政府为供养这些部队而施加的财政压力与新的市场机会，可能共同带来了新的生产格局，以适应新的需求格局。须把花粉资料放到这一更广阔的背景下理解，尤其是安纳托利亚北部和本都地区。那里的人口确实在下降，不妨再以6世纪后期至7世纪锡诺普腹地聚落数量锐减为例。
表面上看，某些产品的相对产量降低了，实际上可能只是生产者按人口大幅减少后的需求相应调整了生产。

Armies require above all grain and livestock, the latter both for transport (horses, mules, and donkeys) as well as for food (cattle, sheep, goats, dairy, produce), along with other staples— wine, oil, and cheese, for example. Given the increased demand from military units on the Anatolian provinces from the 640s and 650s, therefore, it is perhaps not surprising to find that the palynological data indicates the expansion across this period of the simplified mixed cereal-pastoral regime that we have described in the preceding chapter. Several factors coincide to suggest an explanation. On the one hand, we have a situation clearly indicated in the archaeological record in which those areas that had formerly depended on a fairly international market for their specialized produce— wine, olives, and oil in particular— were faced with a considerably reduced demand. Minor shifts in climate may have made continuation of the traditional agriculture difficult or impossible, although as we have seen the proxy data discussed in the preceding chapter do not indicate such a shift in Anatolia at this point. At the same time, the arrival of larger than usual numbers of soldiers in many districts and on a more or less permanent basis meant an increased demand for produce such as wheat as well as livestock. Fiscal pressure exerted by the government to support these troops, together with new market opportunities, may thus have combined to generate new patterns of production to meet the new patterns of demand. The pollen data need to be understood within this broader context, especially for northern Anatolia and the Pontic region where, in a situation of real demographic down-turn (compare once again the dramatic later sixth- to seventh-century collapse of settlement numbers in the hinterland of Sinope, for example),
what may appear to be a reduction in relative levels of production might in fact conceal a proportionate response by producers to meet the needs of a much smaller population.
这也很可能正是当时财政术语变化所反映的情况。原来指强制收购的词语，逐渐有了定期征派的含义。对于已经种植谷物的农人来说，把原种其他作物的土地改种谷物并非轻而易举，但国家对某些产品的需求，或某种财政激励，比如维持已有的谷物税率，却提高某些其他作物的税率，都是可以有效促成改变的手段。
鉴于前几章所述帝国财政所能触及的范围，以及政府驻省官员深入各地的能力，有意采取这种干预措施完全可行，也足以影响地主和农人的耕作策略。这些变化都发生在约650年至约700年之间，至少提示了君士坦丁堡政府为应对困局可能采取的某些措施。

And this is what the shifting fiscal terminology of the period—as words originally signifying compulsory purchase came to have the meaning of regular imposition— may well reflect. While it is not an entirely straightforward matter for farmers already growing cereals to pull land hitherto exploited for other crops into cereal production, a state demand for certain products, or a fiscal incentive— maintaining tariffs on cereals at existing levels, for example, while increasing tax-rates on some other types of crop— are effective forcing agents.

Given the effectiveness of the imperial fiscal reach and the penetrative capacities of the government’s provincial representatives described in earlier chapters, we should not doubt that such a deliberate intervention was possible and that it could impact on the agricultural strategies employed by landowners and farmers. The coincidence of all these developments over approximately the period ca. 650 to ca. 700 is, at the very least, suggestive of some of the measures taken by the Constantinopolitan government to address the difficult situation it faced.
